learning_outcomes.description: Analyze algorithmic time and space complexity using recurrence relations and Master Theorem.
Implement linear data structures (arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues) and non-linear data structures (binary search trees, AVL trees, heaps).
Apply graph algorithms (BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Kruskal) to solve real-world routing and optimization problems.

weeks.topic: Algorithmic Analysis, Asymptotic Notation, and Recursion.
Arrays, Dynamic Vectors, and Singly/Doubly Linked Lists.
Stacks, Queues, and Applications in Parsing and State Exploration.
Comparison Sorts (MergeSort, QuickSort) and Non-Comparison Sorts (Radix, Counting).
Binary Search Trees, Tree Balancing, and AVL Rotations.
Priority Queues, Binary Heaps, and Huffman Coding.
Hash Tables, Collision Resolution Strategies, and Universal Hashing.
Graph Representation, Breadth-First Search (BFS), and Depth-First Search (DFS).
Minimum Spanning Trees (Prim, Kruskal) and Single-Source Shortest Paths (Dijkstra).
